top.headline: Trump Enters the Anger Stage Over the GOP's Midterm Wipeout
top.blurb: After days of silence following Tuesday's rout, Trump began reposting false claims that Democrats "materialized 20 million new votes" and shared an AI-generated cartoon of UFC fighters beating up journalists. Dana White has reportedly declined the press secretary job Trump offered him, and with Democrats now controlling the House's purse strings, Trump's pet projects — a triumphal arch, a new ballroom — look newly vulnerable.

top.headline: Missouri Voters Just Made Their Ballot Initiatives Nearly Impossible for Lawmakers to Undo
top.blurb: Missouri's Amendment 6 now requires 80% support in both legislative chambers, plus a statewide vote, before lawmakers can touch a citizen-passed initiative — protection that covers the 2024 abortion-rights amendment. Democrats also flipped 16 state House seats the same day, though Republicans still hold every statewide office; the amendment's chief opponent, Secretary of State Denny Hoskins, predicts a court challenge.

top.headline: The 'Latinos Are Republicans Now' Theory Didn't Survive the Midterms
top.blurb: A record 14.5 million Latino voters turned out Tuesday and helped elect Texas's first Latina governor, a Democrat — undercutting the post-2024 narrative that Latino men had permanently shifted toward MAGA. Analysts point to gas and grocery prices and anger at ICE raids, noting nearly 80% of Latino voters are working class and could swing back if Democrats don't deliver economically.

top.headline: As Maharashtra's Traditional Midwives Age Out, Rural Mothers Are Left With Nowhere to Turn
top.blurb: Palghar's soyeen, Warli midwives now mostly in their fifties to seventies, have been sidelined since local deliveries shifted to health centres two decades ago, and younger women have largely stopped learning the practice. The district has recorded more than 450 maternal deaths since 2011, and a 2025 study found 10 of 12 recent deaths traced to hospitals unable to handle complications.

top.headline: Karnataka's Congress Government Outspent Its BJP Predecessor by Rs 142 Crore on Advertising
top.blurb: Assembly replies and an RTI obtained by Newslaundry show Karnataka spent Rs 473.46 crore on publicity over three years, or roughly Rs 43 lakh a day, with Rs 240 crore going to promote the state's five Guarantee welfare schemes. A September ad also featured former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah's photo, which Newslaundry notes falls outside Supreme Court exceptions meant for sitting officials only.

top.headline: Trump Says He'll Raise Iran With Xi and Putin at Next Week's APEC Summit
top.blurb: Trump said Washington's land blockade on Iran's supply routes is now in effect and that further strikes are "highly unlikely" if talks on Tehran's nuclear programme and the Strait of Hormuz progress, ahead of meetings with Xi Jinping and Putin at next week's APEC summit. Iran has threatened to "rain down hell" if the US resumes attacks, and a drone strike has separately knocked out an Iraqi Kurdistan gas field.

top.headline: More Than 200,000 March in Amsterdam's Fourth 'Red Line' Protest Against Israel
top.blurb: Amnesty International's Dutch branch says over 200,000 people marched Sunday demanding tighter trade restrictions and an end to arms sales to Israel, citing a Gaza war that has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians, including 21,000 children, since October 2023. Prime Minister Rob Jetten skipped the march but said his government is raising diplomatic pressure on Israel, after banning settlement-product imports in February.

top.headline: Israel's Eisenkot Gets Six Weeks to Form a Government — and Won't Rule Out Netanyahu
top.blurb: President Isaac Herzog formally tasked former army chief Gadi Eisenkot with building Israel's next coalition after October's election left neither bloc a majority, and Eisenkot says he's open to including Netanyahu. With Arab-led parties ruled out, Eisenkot likely needs the ultra-Orthodox Shas and United Torah Judaism, numbers watched closely in the capital where neither alliance alone yet clears 61 seats.

top.headline: New Zealand's ODI Squad Thins Further as Tickner Joins Injury List Ahead of Hamilton
top.blurb: Blair Tickner will miss New Zealand's next two ODIs against India after being struck while batting in Wellington, with Kristian Clarke drafted in as cover; Matt Henry and the already-sidelined Lockie Ferguson are also out. India lead the five-match series 2-0 heading into Tuesday's third ODI in Hamilton, with New Zealand's Test regulars already released to prepare for World Test Championship duty.

top.headline: 'Possible Love' Review: Lee Chang-dong's Venice Winner Is a Quiet Indictment of the Limits of Compassion
top.blurb: Lee Chang-dong's Netflix film, which won two awards at Venice, follows two couples from different economic classes — played by Sul Kyung-gu, Jeon Do-yeon, Cho Yeo-jeong and Zo In-sung — drawn together by a documentary project. Critic Nandini Ramnath calls it a quietly damning study of wealth and empathy's limits, with an overlong finale the film's one real flaw.

top.headline: 'Akka' Creator Dharmaraj Shetty on Building a Matriarchal World for Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte
top.blurb: Shetty's five-episode Netflix series, produced by YRF's digital arm, follows rival women vying for control of a fictional matriarchal coastal town and stars Tanvi Azmi, Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte.

bengal.headline: Presidency University Expels Two Students Over Defaced Vivekananda Poster
bengal.blurb: An inquiry found the two women had written abusive words on a Vivekananda poster put up by the ABVP, prompting expulsion and a campus ban; the SFI called the punishment too harsh.

bengal.headline: ISKCON-Linked Annamrita Gets Nod to Take Over School Meals Statewide
bengal.blurb: Bengal approved expanding Annamrita's centralised-kitchen model for PM POSHAN meals to all districts, drawing criticism over its vegetarian-only menu and the fate of self-help group women who currently cook.

travel.headline: Greece's Own Buried Bronze Age City Tells a Story Four Times Bigger Than Krakatoa
travel.blurb: Santorini's Thera eruption buried the Bronze Age settlement of Akrotiri under 200 feet of ash around 1600 BCE, releasing roughly four times Krakatoa's output; only 10% has been excavated since 1967.

travel.headline: Kenya Launches $160 Million, 10-Year Push to Protect Wildlife Across 31 Counties
travel.blurb: Thamani Asili, backed by Kenya's government and conservation partners, targets 17.3 million hectares and projects it will benefit 1.6 million people and create nearly 22,800 jobs over the decade.

happy.headline: A Pompeii Wardrobe Sealed for 2,000 Years Finally Opens, Spilling Perfume, Amulets and a Grape-Charm Necklace
happy.blurb: Inside, archaeologists found a bronze lamp, tweezers, 38 coins and a necklace strung with two dozen tiny amulets shaped like gods, hands and grape clusters; the park's director says the ordinary objects "bring us closer to their daily life."

tech_top.headline: Nvidia's Board Investigates Jensen Huang Over an Affair With a Woman US Intelligence Calls a Chinese Asset
tech_top.blurb: Huang admitted in a staff memo to an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive a US policy memo alleges China's Ministry of State Security recruited to target him; Nvidia's board says it has "no reason to believe" secrets were compromised and that Huang supports an independent review.
tech_top.pm_note: A $4.5 trillion company's valuation is now entangled with one executive's personal conduct and a national-security memo he can't control — a sharp reminder that founder-dependent companies carry a risk line item most cap tables don't price in.

tech_top.headline: A Decade-Long Grid Mystery Traced to Batteries Checking Their Charge on the Same Clock Tick
tech_top.blurb: German researchers found that internet-synchronized uninterruptible power supplies and grid batteries all check their charge at the same moment each minute, creating a visible frequency wobble that has roughly quadrupled in Ireland since 2016 as data centers grew. The fix: manufacturers should randomize the timing instead of syncing to the clock.
tech_top.pm_note: This is a reminder that synchronized clocks are an externality: a design choice that's invisible and harmless at small scale becomes a systemic risk once enough devices adopt it, and nobody owns the fix until regulators or standards bodies step in.

tech_more.headline: Tesla Will End Cybertruck Production in 2027 After Selling a Fraction of Its Reservations
tech_more.blurb: Musk confirmed the Cybertruck's production run ends in 2027; despite roughly 1 million early reservations, industry estimates put actual sales near 71,000 since 2023, well short of its promised 500-mile range and sub-$40,000 price.

tech_101.text: The exposure a company carries when its value depends heavily on one individual's judgment or reputation — why a personal scandal involving Nvidia's CEO can move a $4.5 trillion valuation, independent of whether any secret actually leaked.

What happens when many independent devices are all set to act on the same clock tick — like batteries worldwide checking their charge at the top of every minute — turning an invisible design choice into a visible, shared-system disturbance.

science.headline: A Liquid-Assisted Crystal Trick Sets a New Record for Clean Perovskite Solar Cells
science.blurb: Sungkyunkwan University researchers used a chloride-and-zinc-halide mixture that melts at grain boundaries to grow larger, lower-defect perovskite crystals, reaching the lowest surface recombination velocity ever reported for the material. The resulting films produced solar cells at 25.9% certified efficiency and LEDs at 26.1% external quantum efficiency.

science.headline: Three Meteor Showers and a Run of Supermoons Light Up November's Sky
science.blurb: November brings the Southern and Northern Taurids and the Leonids, with the Taurids capable of bright fireballs, plus a close Mars-Jupiter pairing before dawn on the 15th and 16th. The month closes with the first of three consecutive supermoons on November 24, while Voyager 1 nears a one-light-day distance from Earth.

science.headline: Engineered Immune Cells Wipe Out a Deadly Childhood Brain Cancer in Every Mouse Tested
science.blurb: UCSF's B-SYNC CAR-T cells stay dormant until they reach the brain, then eliminated diffuse midline glioma — a nearly always-fatal pediatric cancer — in two mouse models, with treated mice also rejecting new tumor cells introduced seven weeks later. Human trials could begin at UCSF as early as April 2027.

philosophy.headline: AuDHD Is a Life of Two Halves — and Psychiatry Only Recently Allowed It to Exist
philosophy.blurb: Sarah Hendrickx explains that the combined autism-ADHD diagnosis, AuDHD, only became namable after the DSM-5 dropped its 2013 ban on diagnosing both at once, though an estimated 50-70% of autistic people also have ADHD. She argues the constant tension between autism's need for routine and ADHD's pull toward novelty also produces real creativity, once it's understood rather than pathologized.

philosophy.headline: We Need a Word for Grief That Isn't About Death
philosophy.blurb: Derek van Zoonen argues grief follows any loss that disrupts someone's identity, not just bereavement — an estranged parent, a faded friendship — yet Western culture and psychiatry recognize almost none of it, a gap he calls disenfranchised grief. Left unnamed, he writes, that "love with nowhere to go" tends to resurface later as physical or emotional symptoms instead.

philosophy_101.text: Grief that follows a real loss — an estrangement, a friendship's end — which culture and medicine don't officially recognize as grief, leaving people to carry it without ritual, language, or support.

Psychiatry's old rule against diagnosing two overlapping conditions, like autism and ADHD, in the same person at once — dropped only in the DSM-5 in 2013, which is why naming the combined AuDHD experience is so recent.
